Dīpaṅkaravyākaraṇa-nā._Ma._Sū.
Bud. by Viśuddhasim3ha an. Jñānagarbha. Kanjur Kyoto 855.

-1055 A. D.; native of Bengal; son of Kalyāṇaśrī an. Śrī Prabhā (Prabhāvatī); studied under Jitāri, Ratnākaraśānti an. Dharmakīrti (II); was the adhyakṣa of Vikramaśīlavihāra; teacher of Prajñākara (a. of C. on Bodhicaryāvatāra); reformed Buddhist faith in Tibet; the order founded by him came to be known a. yellow cap sect or the virtue practicers; acted a. a peace-maker between emperor Nayapāla an. the Kālacūri king Karṇa; was a contemporary of Bhūsuka an. Dharmakīrti; a. of several works in Sanskrit an. Tibetan (now preserved only in Tibetan translations).
For a detailed account of his life an. activities both in India an. Tibet see P. Bose, Indian Teachers of [Page061-b] Buddhist Universities p.. 66-79. Adyar, 1923; S. Dutt, Buddhist Monks an. Monasteries of India p.. 362-71, London, 1962; also A. K. Warder, Indian Buddhism p. 489.
